title: Legal Principles of Appeal
summary: Outlines legal principles applied by the Court regarding appeals, including the evaluation of uncontroverted facts.
content:
Appeal principles
Pursuant to ss 420 and 423 of the Act, a Full Court has jurisdiction to determine appeals from judgments of the Court constituted by a single judge. Section 425 of the Act provides that: ‘In an appeal, the Court shall have regard to the evidence given in the proceedings out of which the appeal arose, and has power to draw inferences of fact and, in its discretion, to receive further evidence, . . .’
